newsitem.title: PERU: Peru names 9 firms interested in Oct 23 oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru names 9 firms interested in Oct 23 oil sale.

text.p: Peru named Thursday nine foreign oil companies interested in taking part in the October 23 auction of oil block X/XI, which has proven reserves of 60 million barrels of crude oil.

The interested firms were China's state oil company Sapet; Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp, YPF, Tecpetrol and Compania Perez Companc the United States' Occidental Petroleum Corp, Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co. and Pennzoil Co., and Canada's Norcen Energy Resources Ltd., government privatization official Guillermo Seminario said in an interview.
All these companies have bought basic information packages about the state-run Petroperu asset and its auction procedures, he said.
The United States' Mobil Corp had also bought the information but was not likely to enter the auction, according to Seminario.
The minimum bid price for the auction will be set next week, he added.
The winner of the auction will buy the rights to explore and develop the oil block, which lies 720 miles (1,150 km) north of Lima in the Talara region.
The block currently produces 17,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from its roughly 47,000 hectare area, officials said.
Petroperu also owns a refinery in the Talara region, which it plans to auction as part of the state company's piecemeal sell-off.
In the last auction in August, Mobil bought Petroperu's lubricants unit, Petrolube, for $18.9 million.
This sale followed the company's June auctions, when the government sold a 60 percent stake in the La Pampilla refinery near Lima and the rights to develop oil block 8/8X in the northeastern jungle.
A consortium led by Spain's Repsol SA bought the La Pampilla stake for $180.5 million, and a consortium led by Pluspetrol won the oil block with a bid of $142.2 million.
